title: The Tide That Isn't
question: What makes a tsunami different from an ordinary sea wave?
hook: A wave that can affect a whole ocean basin may arrive looking like nothing more than a tide rising too fast.
idea: Tsunamis come from large, sudden displacements of water rather than wind or tides, which gives them very long wavelengths and enormous reach.

beats.prompt: Far offshore, an underwater landslide suddenly shoves a huge volume of water aside. What happens?

choices.label: It can set off a tsunami
Nothing, since only earthquakes make tsunamis
choices.feedback: Earthquakes are the usual cause, but landslides, eruptions and other disturbances that displace water can do it too.

choices.label: It changes the timing of the tides
choices.feedback: Tides come from the pull of the Moon and Sun, not from shoved water.

choices.label: It just makes ordinary wind waves
choices.feedback: Ordinary waves come from wind; displacing a large volume of water is what makes a tsunami.

beats.explain: A tsunami forms whenever a large volume of water is suddenly displaced, and landslides are one of the ways this happens.

beats.prompt: Sort each into what it sets in motion
items: Pull of the Moon and Sun
beats.explain: Tsunamis come from events that displace water; normal waves come from wind and tides from the gravity of the Moon and Sun.

beats.prompt: Put these moments in tsunami history in order
items: Oldest human record of a tsunami, at Potidaea
Thucydides argues ocean earthquakes cause tsunamis
The Indian Ocean tsunami kills around 230,000
beats.explain: Potidaea was 479 BC, Thucydides wrote around 426 BC, Alexandria was hit in 365 AD, and the Indian Ocean tsunami struck in 2004.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong; which?
steps: A coastal town is hit by the first wave of a tsunami.
Tsunamis generally arrive as a series of waves.
The waves in that series can be minutes to hours apart.
So once the first wave has passed, the danger is over.
beats.explain: Because tsunamis come as a wave train with periods of minutes to hours, more waves can follow the first one.
